newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends down after Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends down after Greenspan.

text.p: The Mexican overnight Cetes rate reversed earlier increases to close down 50 basis points at 23.00 percent on Tuesday in step with U.S. long bond rates, traders said.
"Rates opened under pressure and stayed up for quite a while. Nonetheless, one big player flooded the market with liquidity and that brought rates down," a trader said.
Dealers said rates opened up at a session high of 24.25 percent on caution ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan giving testimony to the Senate Budget Committee.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 100 basis points at 24.50 percent.
Traders recalled comments by Greenspan in early December saying asset market valuation was a possible case of "irrational exhuberance" that made international markets wobble.
Greenspan's testimony on Tuesday relieved the market, dealers said, and yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds declined to 6.78 percent in late trade from an early high of 6.89 percent.

"Once Greenspan spoke, rates calmed down and the dollar firmed up. Furthermore, as this is (primary) auction day, it lends itself to those who keep secondary rates down so as to keep primary hikes in check," a trader said.

A Reuters survey of nine Mexican money market dealers showed that they expected Banco de Mexico to assign bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury Certificates) at an average of 23.03 percent, which would be an increase of five basis points from last week's auction.
"The forex market has been stable, so if rates do go up, it will be very slightly," a dealer said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso closed 0.35 of a centavo firmer at 7.7965/7.7995 per dollar.
Banco de Mexico drained 8.105 billion pesos in liquidity through six auctions to buy paper, which it assigned at between 24.65 percent and 25.40 percent.
Traders said government spending had substantially raised liquidity in the system.
Liquidity of 405 million pesos was expected to flow back into the system on Wednesday.
